description: Bridging Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energy on the Rutile TiO2(110) Surface (P4_2/mnm)
user_prompt: Compute the formation energy of a bridging oxygen vacancy on the rutile TiO2(110) surface (P4_2/mnm). Optimize both the clean slab and the slab with one bridging O removed, then compute E_vf = E(defective) - E(clean) + 1/2 * E(O2). Report E_vf in eV.

references: Morgan & Watson, J. Phys. Chem. C 113, 7322 (2009)
Kowalski, Camellone, Nair, Meyer & Marx, Phys. Rev. Lett. 105, 146405 (2010)
method.modeling: Rutile TiO2(110), non-polar stoichiometric termination; slab of >= 4 O-Ti-O trilayers with the bottom layers fixed, vacuum >= 12 A, dilute defect (4x2 surface cell). Remove one bridging (2-fold) surface O, relax both clean and defective slabs.
method.rationale: Value 3.7 eV is the bridging-O vacancy formation energy on rutile TiO2(110) at GGA(+U). Morgan & Watson 2007 (GGA+U, U_eff(Ti 3d)=4.2 eV) report the neutral bridging vacancy at 3.66 eV, and their 2009 JPCC study extends it across the rutile facets. CRITICAL: removing a bridging O leaves two electrons that should localize onto two Ti 3d states (Ti^4+ -> Ti^3+), so +U is needed for the correct Ti^3+ polaron picture. The +/-0.30 eV tolerance absorbs vacancy concentration, slab thickness, U value, and the ~0.4 eV PBE O2 overbinding error.
